## Natural history notes

A crustose lichen characterized by a thin gray to greenish-gray thallus with striking red to pinkish-red bands or patches that help give it a “red-belted” appearance. In Florida, it is found growing on palm trunks and other smooth or lightly textured bark in humid subtropical habitats such as hammocks, swamps, mangroves, shaded forests, parks, and landscaped areas. Like other lichens, it is a symbiotic association between a fungus and photosynthetic partner, growing tightly attached to bark and obtaining moisture and nutrients from the air rather than feeding on the tree itself.
